nodes.name: Every five minutes
nodes.notes:
Five minutes rather than nightly, and this is the opposite decision from training_materialise -- worth saying why, because the two look alike.

The materialiser exists for the day nothing happens: a slot is a weekly rule, so the far edge of the horizon has to be filled even on a quiet week, and that is a once-a-night job. This one exists for the day something DOES happen and the immediate path missed it. `knowledge.LinkAdded` starts the reading at once, which is what makes SC-001's three minutes achievable; this catches the cases where that did not run -- a worker killed mid-pipeline, a relay that was down when the event passed, a model that was not answering. FR-016 says an entry left mid-read must come back on its own, and `knowledge.stuckAfterMinutes` defaults to 30, so a pulse measured in hours would make that promise a lie.

It is also what stamps the `knowledge.ingest` heartbeat. FR-017 wants a stopped pipeline to be visible, and a heartbeat only exists if something stamps it -- there is nothing for the per-link route to stamp. `/health` reads the stamp after `ops.staleAfterMinutes`, which is fifteen, so a five-minute pulse gives it three chances before it cries wolf.

A pass with an empty queue costs one indexed query and returns zeroes; it needs no claimed date, because the drain claims by moving each link's state out of `queued` and a second pass therefore finds nothing to take.

nodes.name: Run Now
nodes.notes: The way a person drains the queue without waiting for the next tick, and the way the phase gate does it -- calling /internal/* directly is the right thing for a gate to do, and it is also what leaves the automation itself untested, which is the hole the heartbeat rule exists to cover. Unconditional on purpose: it takes no input and the drain is idempotent.

nodes.name: Drain
nodes.notes:
`BOTVY_SERVICE_TOKEN` and `BOTVY_API_BASE` are the names the other four cron workflows read and the names compose sets -- the pair once disagreed (`BOTVY_INTERNAL_TOKEN` in compose, `BOTVY_SERVICE_TOKEN` here), which is an empty `Bearer ` and a silent 401 nobody noticed for days. Reading them at all needs `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE: 'false'`, which compose sets: n8n blocks `$env` inside node expressions by default, and until that was set every execution of every cron workflow here failed with `access to env vars denied`.

Ten minutes of timeout, because one pass reads up to fifty links and each one is a fetch plus several calls to the local model -- on a 3B model at 8K context that is minutes, not seconds, and the whole point of doing it here is that nobody is waiting.

`retryOnFail` is OFF, which is the one place this workflow differs from the other four. The drain is not idempotent in the way their passes are: a retry would start a *second* concurrent drain against the same queue, and the in-process guard that makes that harmless lives in one worker process rather than in n8n. There is nothing to gain either way -- a link the failed pass left alone is still `queued` and the next tick, five minutes away, takes it.

`neverError` is off deliberately. A 401 or a 500 has to FAIL here so the error workflow fires and the heartbeat `knowledge.ingest` goes stale, which is what /health reports after fifteen minutes.

nodes.name: Counts
nodes.notes: Kept as the execution's output so n8n's own log is the record of what each pass did. A steady-state tick is all zeroes except `ms`. A non-zero `requeued` is worth reading: it means a worker died holding a link, and those links' attempt counts are deliberately untouched -- a machine that failed is not a link that failed (FR-016). A non-zero `failed` is a source that refused us, and the reason is on the row where the member can read it.
